title: Drumming on the pot
hook: at his wife's death Zhuangzi is found singing, and explains that he grieved, then saw the seasons turning (Zhuangzi 18)

segments.voice: Yesterday, on the bridge, Zhuangzi knew the joy of fish. Your line was I know it from the bridge. What did you know just by being there? Day fifty-four.

Today's story is about grief, so let's go gently. If you're carrying a fresh loss right now, you're welcome here exactly as you are, and nothing in this story asks you to feel any particular way. Here's what happens. Zhuangzi's wife has died. They'd been together for many years. She raised their children with him, and grew old beside him. His old friend Huizi, the one who argued with him on the bridge, comes to the house to pay his respects. And he finds Zhuangzi sitting on the ground, legs sprawled out, banging on a clay pot like a drum, and singing. Today's story is drumming on the pot.
screen: `A STORY ABOUT GRIEF.` → `HUIZI COMES TO MOURN.` → `ZHUANGZI IS SINGING.`

segments.voice: Huizi is shocked. She lived with you, he says. She raised your children. She grew old with you. It would be enough not to weep for her. But drumming on a pot and singing? Isn't that going too far? And Zhuangzi answers, and his answer starts with grief. When she first died, he says, do you think I didn't grieve? Of course I did. He grieved. The story says so plainly. But then, he says, I looked back to her beginning. Before she was born, there was no life. Before that, no body. Before that, not even breath. Then, somewhere in the great mystery of things, there was a change, and there was breath. The breath changed, and there was a body. The body changed, and there was life. And now there's been another change, and she has died. It's like the turning of the four seasons: spring, summer, autumn, winter. She's lying at rest now, in the great room of the world. If I followed her crying and wailing, it would show I didn't understand how things go. So I stopped. Different traditions, and different families, grieve in very different ways, and this story doesn't rank any of them. It's not a rule that we shouldn't cry. Zhuangzi cried. It's what he found on the far side of crying: a way of seeing his wife's life as part of something larger, still moving, like a year. Winter isn't the year going wrong. It's the year. And the pot and the song were what he had left to give her.
screen: `ISN'T THAT GOING TOO FAR?` · `DO YOU THINK I DIDN'T GRIEVE?` · `BREATH, BODY, LIFE, CHANGE.` · `LIKE THE FOUR SEASONS.` · then, large: `SEASONS TURN.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: sit with one loss as a season. Settle, and breathe. Choose a loss that feels right for today. It can be small: a place you moved from, a friendship that faded, a pet. If a big loss is too near, choose a small one, or simply breathe. Remember its spring, when it began. Its summer. Its autumn. And let it be winter now, without forcing anything. If tears come, let them. Zhuangzi had his too. The bell holds the time.
Drumming on the pot. Zhuangzi grieves his wife, then sings, seeing her life as a turning of the seasons. Today's word.
Your line: seasons turn. Today, look for one sign of the season outside, a leaf, the light, the air, and let it remind you of Zhuangzi's turning year. Day fifty-four.

howItsDone: Taoist readers take Zhuangzi's drumming as a teaching about accepting death as part of the transformation of all things; readers from traditions that mourn in very different ways read it too, as one man's path through grief rather than a rule.

fork.setup: you're Huizi. you've come to comfort your friend after his wife's death, and you find him banging a pot and singing. what do you do?
options: tell him it's going too far.
fork.reveal: Huizi says it would be enough not to weep, but singing is too much. Zhuangzi answers: I did grieve. then I saw the seasons turning.

original.note: Chinese, gǔ pén ér gē: drumming on the pot and singing, the phrase that names this story.

trapdoor: what you thought: a man who didn't care that his wife died.
what it means: he grieved, and on the far side of grief he saw her life as part of a turning year.
what a scholar hears: Zhuangzi chapter eighteen, Perfect Happiness: from no life, to breath, to body, to life, to death, like the four seasons.

notes: Zhuangzi 18 paraphrased closely, not quoted. 'Breath' renders qi; 'the great room of the world' paraphrases the text's image of her lying at rest in a vast chamber. Confirm.

Sensitive topic: the hook and practice explicitly allow any response to grief, suggest a small loss if a big one is too near, and the teach says the story isn't a rule against crying and ranks no way of mourning.
Chinese 鼓盆而歌 (gǔ pén ér gē): confirm. The 'pot' is a basin or clay vessel (盆).
